goal_text: (Reused from research_synth_015) Compare RNN, LSTM, and Transformer architectures on their ability to handle long-range dependencies, computational parallelism, and memory requirements.
ground_truth: RNNs process sequences serially and suffer from vanishing gradients, making long-range dependency capture difficult; training is sequential and cannot be parallelized. LSTMs mitigate vanishing gradients using gating mechanisms (input, forget, output gates) but still process serially, limiting parallelism. Transformers use self-attention to capture arbitrary-length dependencies in a single layer; computation is fully parallelizable but memory grows as O(n^2) with sequence length due to the attention matrix.
